about.title: One owner for the whole journey of the grain
about.lead: We are not middlemen. The land, the machinery, the dryers and the elevator are ours. So one company answers for the quality of a consignment, not a chain of five suppliers.
body: CENTRAGRO PLUS LLC farms 14,200 hectares in Vinnytsia region. The black soils of Podillia, a seven-field crop rotation and our own machinery fleet deliver stable yields even in dry years.

Every consignment goes through our laboratory before dispatch: protein, moisture, test weight, falling number, foreign matter. The figures are added to the documents — the partner sees the grain before it has left the yard.

crops.title: Seven crops, one quality standard
crops.lead: Volumes for the 2025/26 season. Hover over a crop to see its consignment specifications.

items.name: Winter wheat
items.alt: Ripe winter wheat ears in backlight
items.text: Soft winter wheat, class 2–3. Protein 12.5–13.8%, moisture up to 14%, falling number from 240 s.

items.name: Grain maize
items.alt: Ripe maize cob with yellow kernels in the field
items.text: FAO 280–340 hybrids. We dry to 14% in our own dryers, so the grain does not heat up in transit.

items.name: Sunflower
items.alt: Field of flowering sunflowers in the sun
items.text: High-oil hybrids. Oil content 46–49%, dispatched mainly to oilseed crushing plants.

items.name: Soybean
items.alt: Ripe soybean pods on the plant, macro shot
items.text: Non-GMO soybean with confirmed origin. Protein 34–37% on a dry matter basis.

items.name: Winter rapeseed
items.alt: Field of flowering winter rapeseed
items.text: Industrial-grade winter rapeseed, oil content 42–45%, low erucic acid content.

items.name: Spring barley
items.alt: Spring barley ears with long awns
items.text: Feed and malting barley. Test weight from 620 g/l, protein to brewery specification.

items.name: Sugar beet
items.alt: Freshly harvested sugar beet at the edge of a field
items.text: Contract growing for sugar plants in the region. Sugar content 17.2% in the 2025 season.

capacity.title: Why the grain arrives in the condition we weighed it in
capacity.lead: Four things we keep in-house instead of handing to contractors.

cards.title: Yields that keep rising
cards.text: Five years running we have lifted wheat yields through crop rotation and precision application. 2022 was a drought year, and we show that one too.

cards.title: Storage and drying
cards.text: Our own grain elevator and three drying complexes. We do not depend on queues at third-party elevators at peak harvest.

cards.title: Logistics with no handovers
cards.text: A fleet of 24 grain trucks, a rail siding and proven routes to the ports. Dispatch in daily consignments.

cards.title: Our own laboratory
cards.text: Every consignment gets its own certificate before dispatch. The figures travel with the grain instead of being argued out on the buyer's weighbridge.

capacity.title_rich: Why grain arrives [[shield]] at the quality we weighed it at

process.title: From field to wagon — five steps
process.lead: One person accountable at every stage. The partner receives a report at each step.

steps.title: Crop rotation and planning
steps.text: Soil analyses for every field, hybrids selected for the specific block, an input application plan for the season.
steps.alt: Young wheat shoots in black soil

steps.title: Precision drilling
steps.text: No-till and strip-till, GPS guidance accurate to 2.5 cm, variable-rate seeding.
steps.alt: Tractor with a wide no-till drill

steps.title: Crop monitoring
steps.text: Drones with NDVI cameras every two weeks, weekly scouting by an agronomist, maps of problem zones.
steps.alt: Agronomist launching a drone over a green field

steps.title: Harvesting and drying
steps.text: Our own combines go into the field on moisture, not on a schedule. Dryers rated at 1,200 t/day are right next door.
steps.alt: Combine harvester unloading grain into a trailer

steps.title: Storage and dispatch
steps.text: A 46,000 t grain elevator, separate storage by class, dispatch by road and rail throughout the year.
steps.alt: Queue of grain trucks beside the silo complex

geo.title: Three clusters within a 40-kilometre radius
geo.lead: A compact land bank means a short haul from field to dryer. The grain has no time to spoil on the way.
geo.note: The furthest field is 38 km from the elevator. The average haul from field to dryer is 14 km.

items.quote: The maize arrives dry, at 13.5–14%. For feed production that is critical: it does not heat up in the silo and does not drag losses along with it.

items.a: From 100 tonnes on spot. Forward contracts start at 500 tonnes and long-term agreements at 2,000 tonnes per season.
First our own laboratory at the elevator — the certificate travels with the consignment. If the buyer prefers, we accept an independent test as final, and you choose the accredited laboratory.

items.q: Can we collect with our own transport?
items.a: Yes. The weighbridge runs 24 hours a day during harvest, with dispatch from 30 tonnes per trip. There is also a rail siding for wagon consignments.
From the basis on the day of dispatch, adjusted for the actual specifications of the consignment. Under a forward contract the price is fixed in the agreement and is not revised.
Yes, an LLC on the general tax system and VAT registered. Full document set: contract, specification, consignment note, laboratory certificate, VAT invoice.
Yes, under a long-term agreement. Hybrid, area and quality parameters are agreed before drilling — a minimum of 500 hectares per contract.

journey.title: Eighteen seasons, one direction
journey.lead: We did not buy a ready-made business — we grew the farm field by field.

items.title: The first 800 hectares
items.text: Leased land in two villages, one old combine and a contract with the local grain elevator.

items.title: Our own machinery
items.text: The first new combine and a wide drill. We stopped depending on contractors at harvest.

items.title: Drying complex
items.text: Two dryers rated at 400 t/day. From that point maize went to partners dry, not "however it came off the field".

items.title: A 30,000 t grain elevator
items.text: Separate storage by class. We began working with flour mills directly, without a trader in between.

items.title: Laboratory and no-till
items.text: Our own laboratory at the elevator. The first 900 hectares moved to no-till.

items.title: 14,200 hectares
items.text: Seven crops, a 46,000 t grain elevator, drying at 1,200 t/day, exports to 14 countries.

mission.title: Four rules we do not bend
mission.lead: They are simpler than they look, and that is exactly why they are still working in their eighteenth season.

items.title: The soil matters more than the season
items.text: A seven-field crop rotation, cover crops, no-till on a third of the area. We plan ten years ahead, not one harvest.

items.title: A figure, not a promise
items.text: Every consignment has a laboratory certificate before dispatch. If a figure falls short — we are the first to say so.

items.title: Agreed means delivered
items.text: A forward price is never reopened. In eighteen seasons we have never failed to deliver a signed volume.

items.title: A short haul
items.text: The furthest field is 38 km from the dryer. The grain has no time to spoil between the combine and the store.
